content: Just reinstalled lean plug-in, created project using project actions. Click into the Main.lean tab, project actions -> build project. Got the message "no active client". If I try to restart the server, it says I don't have a focused lean tab, even though I clicked in a lean file first. Any ideas?
Did you open the project's folder in VSCode, i.e. do you see the folder in VSCode's explorer tab?

Yes

Sent from Proton Mail for Android.
Maybe send a full screenshot of VS Code with the file explorer open and the error visible?

(also, the full output log would be helpful)

Thanks! Could you open the developer console via Cmd+Shift+P, then 'Developer: Open Developer Tools' and then the 'Console' tab? (It likely contains errors, potentially from VS Code itself, but I want to check whether there are any extension-related messages in there)

I don't have a developer tools, just a "web view developer tools". Choosing that doesn't have any noticeable effect.

image.png
You might need to type in "developer tools" instead of "devopentoo" :-)

(Just a bit of context on some of what's going on here: 'No active client' means that there is no language server running at the moment, so the extension can't tell which project to build. Typically, after creating the project and opening that file, Lean should just start working right away and launch a language server for the project of that file, but for some reason it doesn't in this case.)

OK, turns out it's called "Toggle Developer Tools", found it. :-)

This is the log after the sequence:

  1. Start new window
  2. forall->Open Project, open the project
  3. forall->Project Actions->Build Project

image.png
This is after opening a file in your project, right?
It opens Main.lean automatically, but I did click in the file before trying to build

No errors related to our extension that might explain why the Lean client doesn't start on your machine, unfortunately.
(I've also tried reproducing your exact file structure setup on a macOS machine in the mean time, but no luck either, sadly)

Two more absolute shots in the dark:

  • Does disabling all other extensions that aren't the Lean extension, restarting VS Code and then re-trying change anything? (Sometimes, other extensions can interfere with how VS Code dispatches events to extensions, which occasionally breaks things) You can disable extensions by right-clicking them in the extensions sidebar menu and selecting "Disable".
  • Does downgrading the VS Code extension to version 0.0.221 change the situation? You can downgrade the extension by right-clicking on the Lean 4 extension in the extension sidebar menu, selecting "Install Specific Version" and then 0.0.221. Restart VS Code afterwards (or just restart the extension host if the button for it appears)
If none of these work, I'll build a debug build for you so that we can figure out what's going on
OK I tried both of those, no luck - I get the same behavior

Here's a debug build that logs the entire interaction of activating the extension on a specific file:
lean4-0.0.226.vsix
(Obligatory disclaimer regarding this artifact: I am the maintainer of the VS Code extension :-))

You can install it here (and then restart VS Code after installing it):
image.png

The logged interaction will be present in the developer console that you opened via 'Toggle Developer Tools'.
I'll be traveling tomorrow, so I might be a bit slower to respond from now on, but I really hope we can figure this one out.

Thanks! These are the entries that are new with this build:

image.png

Thanks, now I am even more mystified :-)

I forgot to mention - with the same debug build, could you also open another Lean file in the same project and paste the output for that? (I.e. start VS Code > wait for a few seconds until VS Code has started > open Functional/Basic.lean > inspect log)

(also, just to double-check: after opening the Basic.lean file, the language in the bottom right of the VS Code window in the footer panel is shown as "lean4", right?)

OK, here's the screenshot for what's different after opening Functional/Basic.lean:

image.png

But more importantly - you guessed the problem! The language for the file was "lean", not "lean4", even though I uninstalled the old lean extension a long time ago. Once I switched it to lean4 everything started working properly! Thanks so much for your help!

I love it when these obscure issues get resolved. Thanks a lot, both of you, for persevering. I guess this is yet another gotcha that the community should add to its list of possible problems that users can have.

Thanks for helping debug the problem, @Bryn Keller! Now we can also ensure that this horrible initial experience won't affect other users as well :-)

The underlying problem here is that the extension has a bug where it doesn't activate when the language ID is set to lean. This language ID is supported by the VS Code extension (this is indeed an artifact from the Lean 3 times and the time when we transitioned to Lean 4), but we never tell VS Code to associate .lean files with lean - instead, they should always be associated with lean4, as declared in the declarative configuration of the extension. For some strange reason, this does not happen on your machine. The only underlying reasons I could think of for why this is the case is some other extension interfering (e.g. another extension that contributes this association from files to language IDs), which we already excluded, or some strange VS Code bug. I'm not certain about the underlying issue - but we can still fix the problem that it creates: vscode-lean4#738

Kevin Buzzard said:

I love it when these obscure issues get resolved. Thanks a lot, both of you, for persevering. I guess this is yet another gotcha that the community should add to its list of possible problems that users can have.

This is a bug that we can fix. Please don't turn it into a key step in your common troubleshooting, unless someone is stuck on an old VS Code extension version :-)
FWIW, for future troubleshooting, I'd also like to point out to @Snir Broshi and you that it shouldn't be absolutely necessary to open the actual folder of the Lean project you want to work on, except obviously for convenience (e.g. when the folder has a .vscode folder and VS Code should pick that one up, or you want to use the file browser in VS Code). From the perspective of the Lean extension, this doesn't matter anymore - when you look at a file, it will figure out the project that the file is contained in, regardless of which folder is open. If you find any situations where this isn't sufficient, please report them to me as bugs.
